subject: Re: Sudden surge of 429s & higher latency — immediate remediation
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@callista.ai>

Cc: ops@callista.ai
Date: 2029-04-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: sudden spike of 429s and latency increase

Hi Grace / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429 responses to our production requests starting ~07:45 PT this morning. Error rate is ~12% for the past 30 minutes; median latency has risen from ~120ms to ~420ms, and our throughput dropped by ~35%. Our product team rolled a nightly batch this morning that temporarily doubled incoming QPS, but we've not seen this level of rejection before for similar bursts.

Attached are a 10-minute sample of logs (callista_429_sample.log) and the traffic graph. We are seeing a correlation between a set of long-running requests and immediate 429s from the Redwood endpoint.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether any rate-limit or quota changes were applied to our org overnight?
- If this is a burst/quota window problem, can you temporarily raise our burst allowance and/or revert any recent changes? We need something in the next 60 minutes to avoid customer-visible failures.

We appreciate a quick acknowledgment and a target ETA. This is customer-impacting; our oncall is standing by.

— Sanjay
Head of Platform, Callista AI

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@callista.ai>
Date: 2029-04-10T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden spike of 429s and latency increase

On Tue, Apr 10, 2029 at 08:12 AM Sanjay Rao <sanjay@callista.ai> wrote:
> We started seeing a sharp increase in 429 responses...

Quick triage summary:
- Root cause (prelim): Burst-credit accounting mismatch combined with a recent quota normalization job we deployed at 02:00 PT. The normalization reduced per-org burst buffer for accounts exceeding historical 30-day baselines. Callista's nightly batch temporarily pushed them above the baseline; the burst buffer dropped to effectively 0, so the serving runtime started returning 429s once the steady-state rate exceeded the instantaneous bucket.
- Evidence: attached burst_policy_config.yml shows the normalization rule (window=300s, burst_credits=0 for threshold > baseline). The callista_429_sample.log shows 429 responses with x-rate-reason: burst_exhausted.
- Immediate fix (recommended):
  1) Apply emergency override: increase Callista's burst_credits to 600 for 10 minutes and set their transient capacity to +25% for 30 minutes. This should eliminate the 429s during the batch window.
  2) Roll back the normalization for accounts with scheduled nightly batches until we have a proper workload classification.
  3) Create a policy exception ticket so this doesn't auto-apply after the temporary bump (JIRA: INF-9213).

Impact and cost: 25% capacity bump estimated to cost ~$420 for the hour. If approved, we can execute within ~12 minutes — requires an ops-approved capacity bump and confirmation from platform that burst-override is applied.

Action requested: operational approval to apply temporary capacity and burst override now; once applied we'll monitor 15/30/60 minutes and report back.

— Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: burst_policy_config.yml]

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@callista.ai>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-10T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: EXEC ESCALATION: Callista production-impacting 429s — request for emergency capacity + customer remediation plan

Vivek / Laura —

Summary: Callista AI (RD-6721) is experiencing production risk due to a burst-credit normalization rule we rolled out overnight. The rule set burst_credits to 0 for accounts that exceed their 30-day baseline during a configured window. Callista ran a planned nightly batch at 07:30 PT that temporarily doubled their QPS and exhausted burst credits, producing ~12% 429s and elevated latencies.

Immediate asks for executive approval (need reply in next 20 minutes):
- Approve emergency transient capacity bump of +25% for 60 minutes to absorb the scheduled batch (estimated one-hour cost ~$420).
- Approve a short-term goodwill credit if Callista requests it (recommendation: 10% of April invoice) — Marissa to finalize message.
- Approve a temporary policy rollback for the affected cohort: do not apply the normalization to orgs that have scheduled batch windows until we complete classification (engineering lead to own).

Risks of inaction: continued 429s causing customer app errors, potential expansion/renewal impact for Q2, and an executive-level escalation from Callista procurement if we don't resolve quickly.

Plan after approval:
- Aditya will apply override and confirm removal of 429s (T+12 min).
- Monitor 15/30/60 minute windows; report back.
- Post-incident RCA and policy change proposal to be delivered in 3 business days (INF-9213).

Please reply with APPROVE / DENY / MODIFY (and brief rationale). I will execute the approved course and send a customer note.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

[Later that afternoon: Aditya confirmed the override was applied at 08:56 PT and error rates dropped to <0.5% within 10 minutes; Callista acknowledged the temporary fix and asked for the RCA timeline.]
